context: Sachiko and Goro reflect on their long lives with peace.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、長かった、人生。
lines.style: Soft, wondering opening. Sachiko's voice carries the weight of years without heaviness. Warm, reflective pace. A small pause between phrases, like she's gathering the shape of a lifetime into words. Tender nostalgia threading through.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.en: Yes — it truly has been long.
lines.style: Quiet agreement. Goro's tone is steady, philosophical. He doesn't rush the thought. Nodding in his voice, finding his wife's reflection in the mirror of his own life. Gentle and present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: We were able to spend it together — and that makes me happy.
lines.style: Sachiko's gratitude is direct and unguarded. Small breath between clauses. Her voice softens on 'happy,' like she's still discovering this truth. No performance—just the warmth of someone whose life has been witnessed.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: Goro speaks with the simplicity of something earned over decades. Weight on 'truly.' His voice doesn't waver. This is not a question or a confession—it's a statement of fact he's carried long enough to know it's true.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: Our whole family has grown to be fine people.
lines.style: Pride and wonder mixed. Sachiko's voice brightens slightly, energised by the thought of her children and grandchildren. Still warm, but with a lifted quality—the joy of watching something you planted flourish.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.en: Naoko came to the countryside to see us.
lines.style: Goro marks the fact with appreciation. 'Naoko' carries affection. His voice holds the quiet pleasure of being visited, of knowing his daughter made the journey. Gentle acknowledgment of what that choice means.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ひかり、子供たち、可愛い、ね。
lines.en: And Hikari's children — they're so lovely, aren't they.
lines.style: Sachiko's voice lifts with genuine delight. A grandmother's unguarded warmth at the mention of grandchildren. Soft laughter folded into the words. No irony, no distance—just pure affection.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.en: To be able to watch over them all — that's my happiness.
lines.style: Goro's voice settles into something deeper. He's speaking of privilege and responsibility woven together. Slow, steady pace. The words carry the full weight of what it means to be a grandfather who has lived long enough to see it matter.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: I'm grateful — truly grateful — every single day.
lines.style: Sachiko returns to the refrain with fresh sincerity. Each repetition of 'grateful' lands with quiet emphasis. No fatigue, no formula. Her voice trembles slightly on 'every day,' the realisation that ordinary time has been a gift.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.en: With you — until the very end — together.
lines.style: Goro's voice carries both promise and peace. He doesn't rush the line; each phrase breathes. 'Until the end' is not sad—it's the natural shape of a life lived fully. His tone is certain and tender in the same moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: You're such a precious person to me.
lines.style: Sachiko's voice is hushed, intimate. She's not looking away from this truth. Tender and direct. A small exhale before she speaks, like she's steadying herself to say something that matters. No apology in her tone—just love.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: Goro mirrors his wife's honesty with his own. His voice is quiet and complete. He's not adding anything unnecessary. This is the answer she needed to hear, delivered with the certainty of someone who has known this for decades.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: And we'll keep going together — won't we.
lines.style: Sachiko's voice finds a gentle note of closure without finality. Soft question-mark in her tone—an invitation to agree on what they both already know. Hopeful, tender, the warmth of two people folded into one life.
